statements.proof_tex:
Put \(d=|A|-1\), \(g=D_Ah\), and \(J_A=D_A^{\prime}(D_AD_A^{\prime})^{-1}\).  The canonical representative is \(h^\circ=J_Ag\).  The quotient loss
\[
\ell_a(g)=\max_{k\in A}(J_Ag)_k-(J_Ag)_a
\]
is independent of the representative and satisfies on \(K_M=\{g:\lVert g\rVert_2\leq M\}\)
\[
0\leq\ell_a(g)\leq L_M:=2\lVert J_A\rVert_{2\to\infty}M,
\qquad
|\ell_a(g)-\ell_a(g')|\leq2\lVert J_A\rVert_{2\to\infty}\lVert g-g'\rVert_2. \tag{18}
\]
By \(\text{lem:gaussian-quotient-reduction}\), it suffices to certify the experiment \(Y\sim N(g,\Omega)\), \(g\in K_M\).

We first describe exact lower certificates.  Choose a rational grid \(g_1,\ldots,g_S\subset K_M\) and rational prior weights \(w_s\geq0\), \(\sum_sw_s=1\).  For action \(a\), let \(\varphi_\Omega\) denote the centered \(N(0,\Omega)\) density and define the posterior cost density
\[
c_a(y)=\sum_{s=1}^S w_s\ell_a(g_s)\varphi_\Omega(y-g_s). \tag{19}
\]
The Bayes risk of this prior is exactly
\[
V(w,\Omega)=\int_{\mathbb R^d}\min_{a\in A}c_a(y)\,dy. \tag{20}
\]
Indeed, for every randomized selector \(\delta\), Tonelli's theorem applies to the nonnegative bounded integrand and gives Bayes risk \(\int\sum_a\delta_a(y)c_a(y)dy\), minimized pointwise by an action attaining \(\min_ac_a(y)\).  Therefore every outward-downward enclosure of (20) is a valid lower bound for \(G_{A,M}\).  On a rational observation box, directed interval evaluation of (19) and subdivision at action-switching cells encloses the integral.  Omitting the complement is valid for a lower bound because the integrand is nonnegative.

For an upper certificate, store on each rational observation cell a rational action distribution and use a fixed action outside the truncation box.  If \(\overline\lambda\) bounds \(\lambda_{\max}(\Omega)\) on the covariance cell and the box contains \([-T,T]^d\) with \(T>M\), the union bound and the one-dimensional Gaussian tail yield uniformly in \(g\in K_M\)
\[
\Pr_{g,\Omega}\{Y\notin[-T,T]^d\}
\leq2d\,\Phi\!\left(-\frac{T-M}{\sqrt{\overline\lambda}}\right). \tag{21}
\]
Multiplication by \(L_M\) is a certified tail contribution.  On each retained observation cell, interval Gaussian integration gives outward enclosures of the selected-action probability.  If interval posterior costs certify one minimizing action, the cell is marked certified.  Otherwise all possibly minimizing actions are retained and the upper calculation adds the interval width between their largest and smallest posterior costs.  Uniform continuity of the finitely many functions in (19) makes this ambiguous-cell contribution tend to zero as the observation mesh tends to zero, including a region of exact ties, where the true cost difference is zero.

It remains to control parameters and covariances explicitly.  For completeness, if \(A_0=\{dP/dQ\geq1\}\), the log-sum inequality applied to \(A_0,A_0^c\) gives \(\operatorname{KL}(P,Q)\geq d_{\mathrm{bin}}\{P(A_0),Q(A_0)\}\); integrating the second derivative of the binary divergence along the segment between its two arguments gives \(d_{\mathrm{bin}}(u,v)\geq2(u-v)^2\).  Since \(P(A_0)-Q(A_0)=\lVert P-Q\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}\), this proves \(\lVert P-Q\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}^2\leq\operatorname{KL}(P,Q)/2\).  For a fixed covariance with \(\lambda_{\min}(\Omega)\geq\underline\lambda>0\), the equal-covariance Gaussian integral gives
\[
\operatorname{KL}\{N(g,\Omega),N(g',\Omega)\}
=\frac12(g-g')^{\prime}\Omega^{-1}(g-g')
\leq\frac{\lVert g-g'\rVert_2^2}{2\underline\lambda}. \tag{22}
\]
Combining (18) and (22), every rule obeys the computable parameter modulus
\[
|R(g,\delta)-R(g',\delta)|
\leq2\lVert J_A\rVert_{2\to\infty}\lVert g-g'\rVert_2
+\frac{L_M}{2\sqrt{\underline\lambda}}\lVert g-g'\rVert_2. \tag{23}
\]
For two covariance matrices the exact same-mean Gaussian divergence is
\[
\operatorname{KL}\{N(g,\Omega),N(g,\Omega')\}
=\frac12\left[\operatorname{tr}(\Omega'^{-1}\Omega)-d
+\log\frac{\det\Omega'}{\det\Omega}\right]. \tag{24}
\]
Every operation in (24), including inverse and determinant, is interval-evaluated on a branch cell whose eigenvalues are bounded below by \(\underline\lambda\).  Pinsker and multiplication by \(L_M\) turn the resulting outward upper enclosure into a covariance-risk modulus.  Thus (23)--(24) cover every point between rational parameter and covariance grid points.

To prove termination, fix a covariance.  Equicontinuity (23) reduces the compact parameter game to a finite parameter grid with an arbitrarily small error.  For that finite grid, the set of attainable risk vectors is convex and compact: bounded selectors are weakly compact in \(L^2\) under the finite Gaussian-mixture measure, and each risk coordinate is a continuous linear functional.  Separating this set from a strictly lower orthant shows that its minimax value equals the supremum over finite prior weights of the Bayes values (20).  Rational weights are dense in the finite simplex.  Hence a rational prior and a represented Bayes selector have lower and upper risks within any prescribed positive gap.  Equations (21)--(23) show that sufficiently large \(T\) and sufficiently fine rational observation and parameter partitions preserve that gap.  Equation (24) and compactness of the covariance cell give a finite subdivision on which the covariance contribution is smaller than any prescribed remainder.  Assigning, for example, one sixth of \(\varepsilon\) to parameter interpolation, covariance perturbation, truncation, quadrature, ambiguous cells, and final outward rounding proves that exhaustive refinement must eventually verify \(U-L\leq\varepsilon\).

The transcript is logically complete because a checker needs no floating-point trust: it contains the rational matrices and boxes, prior and selector probabilities, directed lower and upper endpoints for (19)--(24), the six error totals, and the final comparison.  The code revision and checksum identify the exact checker bytes; logical validity comes from rechecking the recorded inequalities.  Quasi-Monte Carlo, Sobol, or multistart output is not an input to any bound.

For Bernoulli designs, \(q_k=(Bp)_k\geq\min_\ell B_{k\ell}>0\) uniformly on compact \(\Delta_K\).  Together with positive bounded \(v_A\), this places all quotient covariances in one compact uniformly positive-definite set, which finitely many rational cells cover.  For exact-count designs this argument applies on every compact subset of \(\Delta_A^\circ\), while the zero-rate theorem forbids a uniform positive-definite cell at the boundary.

Finally, the displayed rational matrix follows by substituting \(n=6\) and \((m_1,m_2,m_3)=(1,2,4)\) into the binomial formula.  Summing its columns gives
\[
\frac{3125}{7776}+\frac{3125}{15552}+\frac{125}{15552}=\frac{2375}{3888},
\quad \frac{64+80+20}{243}=\frac{164}{243},
\quad \frac{4+20+80}{243}=\frac{104}{243}.
\]
The second is strictly largest, and division of its entries by \(164/243\) gives \((16/41,20/41,5/41)\).  No optimizer or noncompact risk claim follows from this arithmetic, so none is asserted.

statements.statement:
Fix \(A\), \(M<\infty\), and a compact set of representative local directions whose quotient norms are at most \(M\).  Under \(\mathsf B(p)\), use an independent pilot of size \(m_C\to\infty\) with \(m_C/C\to0\) to estimate \(\widehat\Sigma_{C,A}\), snap it outward to a prespecified rational covariance partition, compute the corresponding compact certificate selector \(\delta_{\varepsilon,A}\), and apply that selector to the calibrated estimator from the remaining clusters.  Uniformly over \(p\in\Delta_K\) and over that compact local set,
\[
\limsup_{C\to\infty}\left\{\sqrt C\,\mathbb E_{(Q^B_{\bar P_{C,h},p})^{\otimes C}}
\left[\max_{k\in A}U_k(\bar P_{C,h})-U_{\delta_{\varepsilon,A}}(\bar P_{C,h})\right]
-U_\varepsilon(v_A,(Bp)_A)\right\}\leq0.
\]
There is a diagonal choice \(\varepsilon_C\downarrow0\), with pilot fraction still vanishing and pilot size diverging, whose Gaussian risk converges uniformly to \(G_{A,M}(v_A,(Bp)_A)\).  The uniformity over \(p\) uses the primitive bound \(\min_{p\in\Delta_K}(Bp)_k=\min_{\ell\in\mathcal K}B_{k\ell}>0\) for every active \(k\).
statements.justification: This turns the compact Gaussian receipt into an implementable calibrated Bernoulli rule with uniform nominal-label control.
statements.gap: Gaussian certificates require a separate bounded-score, cell-positivity, and covariance-snapping transfer to the exact-hit experiment.
statements.consumer: It implements the certified fixed-face selector under Bernoulli saturation labels.
statements.proof_tex:
Let the pilot size be \(m_C\to\infty\) with \(m_C/C\to0\).  By \(\text{lem:exact-hit-factorization}\), uniformly in \(p\in\Delta_K\),
\[
\Pr_p(Z=z)=\frac{(Bp)_k}{M_k}\geq
\frac{\min_{\ell\in\mathcal K}B_{k\ell}}{M_k}>0,
\qquad z\in\mathcal S_k. \tag{25}
\]
All welfare observations are bounded.  Cellwise Chebyshev inequalities, followed by a finite union bound over the fixed collection of target assignments, show that the pilot cell means, variances, hit rates, and hence \(\widehat\Sigma_{C,A}\), are uniformly consistent over \(p\).  Active-slice nondegeneracy and (25) put the quotient covariance in a compact set with eigenvalues bounded away from zero and infinity.

Fix \(\varepsilon\).  Cover that covariance set by the finite rational terminal cells returned by \(\text{thm:gaussian-finite-certificate}\), with boundary conventions assigning every estimated matrix to one cell.  Conditional on the pilot, the main sample contains \(C-m_C\) independent records and is independent of the selected represented rule.  The bounded triangular-array characteristic-function proof underlying \(\text{thm:efficient-exact-hit-bernoulli}\), and the local mean calculation in \(\text{thm:target-tangent-lan-bernoulli}\), are uniform over \(p\) by (25) and over compact representative sets because all third remainders are bounded.  Since the finite represented selector has only finitely many polyhedral or rectangular boundaries, and a positive-definite Gaussian assigns those boundaries probability zero, conditional convergence gives its Gaussian risk.  The finite number of covariance cells makes the convergence uniform over every selector in the receipt.

Also, uniformly on the stated local set,
\[
\sqrt C\left\{\max_{k\in A}U_k(\bar P_{C,h})-U_a(\bar P_{C,h})\right\}
=\max_{k\in A}h_k-h_a+o(1), \tag{26}
\]
by the bounded exponential-family Taylor expansion.  Combining conditional convergence, (26), and the certificate's uniform upper bound gives the displayed limit superior.  The factor \(\sqrt C/\sqrt{C-m_C}\to1\), so the vanishing pilot fraction does not change the covariance.

For each integer \(j\), repeat the argument with \(\varepsilon=1/j\) and a rational covariance mesh fine enough for that receipt.  Choose deterministic thresholds \(C_j\) after which the pilot error and main-sample risk error are at most \(1/j\), and let \(j(C)\uparrow\infty\) sufficiently slowly.  Then \(m_C\to\infty\), \(m_C/C\to0\), and
\[
G_{A,M}\leq U_{1/j}\leq L_{1/j}+1/j\leq G_{A,M}+1/j.
\]
This diagonal rule attains \(G_{A,M}(v_A,(Bp)_A)\) uniformly in \(p\) and on the stated compact local set.

statements.statement:
Fix \(A\), \(M<\infty\), a compact set of representative local directions whose quotient norms are at most \(M\), and a compact subset of \(\{\alpha\in\Delta_K:\min_{k\in A}\alpha_k>0\}\).  Under \(\mathsf{CR}(\alpha)\), take within each active stratum a prespecified pilot count tending to infinity and equal to \(o(C_{C,k})\), estimate \(\widehat\Sigma_{C,A}\), snap it outward to a prespecified rational covariance partition, compute \(\delta_{\varepsilon,A}\), and apply it to the remaining calibrated estimator.  Uniformly over this compact allocation set and compact local set,
\[
\limsup_{C\to\infty}\left\{\sqrt C\,\mathbb E_{Q^{CR}_{\bar P_{C,h},C_C}}
\left[\max_{k\in A}U_k(\bar P_{C,h})-U_{\delta_{\varepsilon,A}}(\bar P_{C,h})\right]
-U_\varepsilon(v_A,\alpha_A)\right\}\leq0.
\]
A diagonal choice \(\varepsilon_C\downarrow0\) attains \(G_{A,M}(v_A,\alpha_A)\) uniformly on that compact allocation set.  No transfer is asserted as an active share vanishes or the active face changes.
statements.justification: This implements the compact selector in the fixed-stratum benchmark on exactly the allocation domain where studentization is uniform.
statements.gap: The fixed-count triangular array needs its own within-stratum pilot argument and cannot borrow boundary uniformity from the iid regime.
statements.consumer: It implements the certified selector under exact-count complete randomization.
statements.proof_tex:
Let the allocation vectors range over a compact subset of the active interior.  Then some \(\rho>0\) satisfies \(C_{C,k}/C\geq\rho/2\) eventually, uniformly for \(k\in A\).  Under assumptions \(\text{ass:cr-label-vector}\), \(\text{ass:cr-label-schedule-independence}\), and \(\text{ass:cr-exact-slices}\), every target assignment in stratum \(k\) has conditional probability \(1/M_k\), and the stratum contains at least \(\rho C/2\) clusters.  A pilot count tending to infinity and equal to \(o(C_{C,k})\) therefore gives, by bounded Chebyshev inequalities and a finite union bound, a uniformly consistent \(\widehat\Sigma_{C,A}\).  The remaining stratum counts divided by \(C\) still converge uniformly to \(\alpha_k\).

The quotient covariance matrices consequently lie in a compact uniformly positive-definite set.  Snap the pilot estimate to the finite rational partition supplied by \(\text{thm:gaussian-finite-certificate}\).  Conditional on the fixed label vector and pilot observations, the main observations are independent across clusters.  The bounded Lindeberg and local-mean calculations in \(\text{prop:efficient-exact-hit-cr-face}\) and \(\text{thm:target-tangent-lan-cr}\) hold uniformly on the compact allocation and representative sets.  As in the Bernoulli proof, every represented selector boundary is null under every positive-definite Gaussian law, and the finite family of receipt selectors makes conditional risk convergence uniform.  The causal-loss expansion (26) is unchanged.  Thus the displayed upper bound follows; the total pilot fraction vanishes because each within-stratum pilot is \(o(C_{C,k})\).

Applying the same slow diagonal construction with \(\varepsilon=1/j\) gives uniform convergence to \(G_{A,M}(v_A,\alpha_A)\).  If an active share tends to zero, pilot consistency is no longer uniform, quotient covariance leaves every compact positive-definite cell, and the Gaussian value diverges by \(\text{lem:gaussian-information-order}\); hence the proof supplies no boundary or changing-face transfer, exactly as stated.

statements.statement: Determine whether \(\mathfrak C_K\) can be completed into one arbitrary-\(\varepsilon\) validated certificate for the noncompact quotient values \(G_A(v_A,r_A)\), uniformly across all partial-tie faces, uniformly positive-definite covariance perturbations, and outer-design limits, while treating a vanishing action-relevant active rate through the proved infinite boundary value rather than evaluating a positive-rate Gaussian formula there.  The required theorem must prove that a screened hierarchical selector, which retains arms near the observed maximum and invokes compact selectors on every retained subset, uniformly approximates the unbounded game and transfers to the calibrated primitive experiments.  A radial truncation alone is not an admissible solution because configurations such as \((0,-a,-M)\) retain a lower-dimensional near-tie game as \(M\to\infty\).
statements.justification: This isolates the genuinely open step needed for one design certificate before the analyst knows the active tie face.
statements.gap: Neither Joo2025 nor Kato2026 proves the required static noncompact screened-selector approximation with changing faces and primitive exact-hit transfer.
statements.consumer: A universal implementation would certify one outer design uniformly over partial ties and admissible covariance perturbations.

statements.statement: For every finite \(A\) with \(|A|\geq2\) and every positive \(v_A,r_A\), the all-selector Gaussian value \(G_A(v_A,r_A)\) equals the infimum over location-invariant selectors \(\delta(x+c\mathbf 1_A)=\delta(x)\).  Every such selector factors measurably through \(D_Ax\), and the quotient observation has law \(N(D_Ah,\Omega_A)\).  The same equivalence holds for \(G_{A,M}\).  Moreover \(G_{A,M}\uparrow G_A\) as \(M\to\infty\).
statements.justification: This removes the spurious information created by observing a centered representative while retaining the common-location nuisance.
statements.gap: The reduction is specialized here to the exact quotient and compact games used by the mechanism theorem.
statements.consumer: It is used by both LAN lower experiments, the two-policy solution, and the compact certificate.
statements.proof_tex:
Write \(d=|A|\), \(\mathbf 1=\mathbf 1_A\), and \(L(h,a)=\max_k h_k-h_a\).  The identity \(L(h+c\mathbf 1,a)=L(h,a)\) holds for every \(c\in\mathbb R\).  For a randomized selector \(\delta=(\delta_a)_{a\in A}\), define its Følner average
\[
\delta_{a,T}(x)=\frac1{2T}\int_{-T}^{T}\delta_a(x+c\mathbf 1)\,dc.
\]
If \(X\sim N(h,\Sigma)\), translation of the Gaussian density and invariance of \(L\) give
\[
R(h,\delta_T)=\frac1{2T}\int_{-T}^{T}R(h+c\mathbf 1,\delta)\,dc
\leq \sup_{u\in\mathbb R^A}R(u,\delta). \tag{1}
\]
The functions \(\delta_{a,T}\) lie in the unit ball of \(L^2_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb R^A)\).  On each member of an increasing sequence of bounded boxes, weak sequential compactness of the Hilbert-space unit ball and a diagonal subsequence give limits \(\bar\delta_a\).  Nonnegativity and \(\sum_a\bar\delta_a=1\) are preserved under weak limits.  For each fixed \(u\), Gaussian density times the bounded loss on a compact parameter neighborhood belongs to \(L^2\) on every box, while its complement is controlled by the Gaussian tail; hence the risk is lower semicontinuous along this diagonal limit.  Equation (1) therefore yields
\[
\sup_uR(u,\bar\delta)\leq\sup_uR(u,\delta). \tag{2}
\]
For fixed \(c_0\), the difference between the averages defining \(\delta_T(x+c_0\mathbf 1)\) and \(\delta_T(x)\) is supported on two intervals of total length at most \(2|c_0|\), so its absolute value is at most \(|c_0|/T\).  Passing to the weak limit first for rational \(c_0\), and then using strong continuity of translations in \(L^2_{\mathrm{loc}}\), shows \(\bar\delta(x+c_0\mathbf 1)=\bar\delta(x)\) almost everywhere for every real \(c_0\).  Choosing a measurable version constant on the fibers gives an invariant selector.  Thus (2) proves that restricting to invariant selectors does not increase the minimax value; the reverse inequality is immediate because invariant selectors are a subclass.

By construction, \(D_A\) has rank \(d-1\), kernel \(\operatorname{span}\{\mathbf 1\}\), and a measurable right inverse \(J_A=D_A^{\prime}(D_AD_A^{\prime})^{-1}\).  Hence every invariant measurable function is constant on every fiber of \(D_A\) and factors as \(\tilde\delta(D_Ax)\).  Linear transformation of a Gaussian vector gives
\[
D_AX\sim N(D_Ah,D_A\Sigma D_A^{\prime})=N(D_Ah,\Omega_A).
\]
For nonzero \(u\in\mathbb R^{d-1}\), full row rank and positive definiteness of \(\Sigma\) imply
\[
u^{\prime}\Omega_Au=(D_A^{\prime}u)^{\prime}\Sigma(D_A^{\prime}u)>0,
\]
so the quotient covariance is positive definite.  This also proves the compact-game equivalence.

Finally let \(g=D_Ah\).  The risks of invariant rules depend only on \(g\), and the balls \(\{g:\lVert g\rVert_2\leq M\}\) increase to \(\mathbb R^{d-1}\).  Therefore \(G_{A,M}\) is nondecreasing and bounded above by \(G_A\).  Choose selectors with compact risks within \(1/M\) of \(G_{A,M}\), use the same diagonal weak-compactness argument on quotient observation boxes, and pass to a subsequence along which the values converge.  The limiting selector has risk no larger than \(\lim_MG_{A,M}\) at every fixed \(g\), hence on their union.  Thus \(G_A\leq\lim_MG_{A,M}\), proving \(G_{A,M}\uparrow G_A\).

statements.statement:
For positive \(v_A,r_A\), \(s>0\), and \(r'_A\geq r_A\) coordinatewise,
\[
G_A(v_A,sr_A)=s^{-1/2}G_A(v_A,r_A),\qquad G_A(v_A,r'_A)\leq G_A(v_A,r_A).
\]
If \((1-\xi)r_A\leq r'_A\leq(1+\xi)r_A\) with \(0<\xi<1\), then
\[
(1+\xi)^{-1/2}G_A(v_A,r_A)\leq G_A(v_A,r'_A)\leq(1-\xi)^{-1/2}G_A(v_A,r_A).
\]
The positive-rate value is finite and strictly positive.  Under the lower-semicontinuous boundary definition, if any action-relevant coordinate \(r_i\) is zero, then \(G_A(v_A,r_A)=+\infty\).
statements.justification: This supplies the scale, comparison, continuity, and boundary facts required to optimize on closed design simplices.
statements.gap: The zero-rate conclusion is proved from an action-relevant two-arm subexperiment rather than imposed by convention.
statements.consumer: It certifies optimizer existence and the exact-hit mass lower bound.
statements.proof_tex:
For homogeneity, let \(X=h+\operatorname{diag}(v_k/(sr_k))^{1/2}Z\), put \(\widetilde X=\sqrt sX\) and \(\widetilde h=\sqrt sh\), and use the bijection between selectors \(\delta(x)\) and \(\widetilde\delta(\widetilde x)=\delta(\widetilde x/\sqrt s)\).  The transformed experiment has rates \(r_A\), while
\[
\max_k\widetilde h_k-\widetilde h_a=\sqrt s(\max_kh_k-h_a).
\]
Taking the infimum and supremum proves \(G_A(v_A,sr_A)=s^{-1/2}G_A(v_A,r_A)\).

If \(r'_k\geq r_k>0\), observe the experiment with rates \(r'_A\) and independently add coordinatewise Gaussian noise with variance \(v_k/r_k-v_k/r'_k\).  The result has exactly the rate-\(r_A\) law.  Composing any rate-\(r_A\) rule with this kernel proves \(G_A(v_A,r'_A)\leq G_A(v_A,r_A)\).  Apply this monotonicity to
\[
(1-\xi)r_A\leq r'_A\leq(1+\xi)r_A
\]
and then use homogeneity to obtain the displayed two-sided modulus.

Finiteness follows from the largest-coordinate rule.  If \(i\) is a best arm and \(d_j=h_i-h_j\geq0\), selecting \(j\) requires \(X_j\geq X_i\) for at least one such \(j\), and hence
\[
R(h,\delta_{\max})\leq\sum_{j\ne i}d_j\Phi\!\left(-\frac{d_j}{\sqrt{v_i/r_i+v_j/r_j}}\right)
\leq\kappa\sum_{j\ne i}\sqrt{v_i/r_i+v_j/r_j}<\infty. \tag{3}
\]
For strict positivity, fix \(i\ne j\), set all other coordinates to \(-H\), and give equal prior mass to the two parameter points with \((h_i,h_j)=(d/2,-d/2)\) and \((-d/2,d/2)\).  The other observations have identical distributions at the two points and convey no testing information.  Sending \(H\to\infty\) makes choosing another arm weakly worse than choosing either \(i\) or \(j\).  The likelihood-ratio test is the sign of \(X_i-X_j\), whose error is \(\Phi(-d/a_{ij})\), where
\[
a_{ij}^2=v_i/r_i+v_j/r_j.
\]
The equal-prior Bayes regret is \(d\Phi(-d/a_{ij})\).  Choosing \(d=a_{ij}x\) and maximizing \(x\Phi(-x)\) gives
\[
G_A(v_A,r_A)\geq\kappa a_{ij}>0. \tag{4}
\]

If \(r_i^{(m)}\downarrow0\) while \(r_j^{(m)}\to r_j>0\), (4) tends to \(+\infty\).  If a second coordinate also tends to zero the same conclusion holds.  Thus every positive sequence approaching a rate vector with an action-relevant zero coordinate has liminf value \(+\infty\), and the stipulated lower-semicontinuous boundary value equals \(+\infty\).

sampling_model.design: Exactly one regime is active. In \(\mathsf B(p)\), labels are iid categorical and units are conditionally independent Bernoulli. In \(\mathsf{CR}(\alpha)\), the label vector has fixed counts \(C_{C,k}\) and each cluster is conditionally uniform on its exact-count slice.
sampling_model.units: Observe \(C\) independent equal-size cluster schedules from an unrestricted binary potential-outcome law, with no interference across clusters and arbitrary interference within a cluster.
sampling_model.treatment: The schedule law \(P\) is mapped to observed data by the known kernel \(R_{B,p}\) or the joint fixed-count kernel \(R^{CR}_{C_C}\); scores and influence functions live in the induced observed-law spaces.
sampling_model.overlap: Interior rational saturations make every Bernoulli hit rate positive. Active-face CR results require positive shares only on \(A\); the full-vector CR CLT and all-policy rank theorem require \(\alpha_k>0\) for every reported policy.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Estimate assignment-specific means and variances within realized target cells, average cells uniformly within each exact-count slice, and use a prespecified bounded fallback for empty cells. Covariance-driven selection may use sample splitting.

estimand_functional: \(\widetilde U_C=(M_k^{-1}\sum_{z\in\mathcal S_k}\overline W_z)_{k\in\mathcal K}\), with full covariance \(\Sigma_B^{(K)}\) under \(\mathsf B(p)\) and \(\Sigma_{CR}^{(K)}\) under all-positive-share \(\mathsf{CR}(\alpha)\).

tldr: The headline result prices the loss from implementing exact-count policy ranking through Bernoulli labels: after projecting to any tied-best face, the optimized regret ratio is bounded by the active exact-hit mass and has an exact equality frontier. Separate observed-law theorems establish finite-sample nuisance deletion, full-menu calibrated CLTs, active-face LAN lower experiments, and tie-valid rank inference. The closest same-target estimator is transcribed exactly from Han--Owusu--Shin Appendix-B Eq. (S1); its derived influence variance reveals cross-label, assignment-cell, and Horvitz--Thompson participation losses. A non-symmetric three-policy menu with unequal variances supplies certified optimizer boxes, attained Gaussian risks, and calibrated oracle-to-data transfer. Uniform certification across changing faces and covariance boundaries remains open.

project_justification.gap: Same-target saturation-ranking work uses the nominal-label Horvitz--Thompson estimator in Appendix-B Eq. (S1) and a rule-specific regret envelope; it does not give all-rule nuisance deletion, observed-law target tangents, or a face-specific optimized mechanism-deficiency frontier.
project_justification.niche: Exact-count deployment exposes a known hit polytope \(B\Delta_K\) inside an unrestricted interference model, allowing the assignment mechanism itself to be priced for the same causal target while keeping schedule and observed-data laws distinct.
project_justification.fill: The project makes mechanism loss the sole headline, derives its observed-score and efficiency foundations, proves the exact Han variance comparison, and couples a Joo-informed static Gaussian selector to calibrated cluster data and a certified asymmetric outer design.

related_work: HanOwusuShin2026 is the closest same-target paper. Its Appendix-B Eq. (S1), pp. 40--44, uses the Horvitz--Thompson normalization \(1/(Cp_k)\) and a within-label likelihood ratio; the exact comparison theorem derives its influence variance and strictly refines it through cross-label assignment calibration. HiranoPorter2009 supplies the limit-experiment architecture, but the all-rule nuisance-deletion theorem and legal observed-law exact-hit tangent are specific to this model. BairdBohrenMcIntoshOzler2018 makes saturation shares a design object under a power criterion rather than optimized facewise simple regret. Joo2025 informs the static Gaussian selector; the contribution here is its coupling to the exact-hit polytope, certified asymmetric outer design, and calibrated cluster-data transfer, not a new generic Gaussian minimax construction. Kato2026, arXiv:2506.24007v6 dated 25 July 2026, is Masahiro Kato's adaptive sequential best-arm comparator and only informs the certification architecture. LoombaEckles2026 informs score projection under structured interference. JiangImaiMalani2023 and MogstadRomanoShaikhWilhelm2024 inform the supporting covariance and rank-inversion results. ChanNakamuraSakaiForastiere2023 is nonarchival prior use of cross-label information for a different hypothetical-allocation target. EggerHaushoferMiguelNiehausWalker2022 supplies the prospective Kenya saturation-design consumer.
technical_internal_limitation: Raw hit pooling is not universally efficient when assignment-specific means vary inside an exact-count slice. The four count-one assignment means \((4/5,4/5,1/5,1/5)\) yield \(\rho_1^2=1/4\) and \(\tau_1^2=4/25\). Han--Owusu--Shin Eq. (S1) additionally pays the first-stage Horvitz--Thompson participation term \(U_k^2(1/\eta_k-1)\). The independent \(\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\) target-bit witness instead has \(\tau_k^2=1/4\) and information \(4q_k\); it is a special lower-bound witness, not the general exponential-tilt score construction.
honest_scope: The results concern fixed \(n\), fixed \(K\), equal cluster sizes, distinct interior rational saturations, isolated iid cluster schedules, and exact-slice welfare. Bernoulli-label and exact-count complete randomization are mutually exclusive regimes, and all scores are defined under their induced observed laws. Active-face CR results allow zero inactive shares, but the full-menu CR CLT and rank theorem require every reported share to be positive. At a unique best policy first-order local regret is zero. When \(K=2\), the face game reduces to the classical sign rule and Neyman allocation; assignment-homogeneous slice means eliminate the calibration component but not necessarily the Horvitz--Thompson participation term in Eq. (S1). The finite positive-face Gaussian certificate and asymmetric three-policy design are theorem targets. A single certificate uniform across data-dependent face changes, covariance perturbations, and admissible boundary limits remains open. The Kenya design is a prospective design consumer rather than an authorized reanalysis.
